title: Why you should aim to be a “good enough” parent, with Tim Cavell, PhD, and Lauren Quetsch, PhD

sentences.en: Raising children can be particularly challenging these days.
sentences.zh: 如今，养育孩子可能是一项特别艰巨的挑战。

sentences.en: There are dozens of books and articles offering competing answers to nearly every parenting question you might have.
sentences.zh: 市面上有数以百计的书籍和文章，对你可能遇到的几乎每一个育儿问题都给出了针锋相对的答案。

sentences.en: From how to get your baby to sleep, to how to help siblings get along, to how much screen time is too much, to whether to let your tween attend a sleepover.
sentences.zh: 从如何让宝宝入睡，到如何帮助兄弟姐妹和睦相处，再到屏幕时间多久才算过长，以及是否该让你的青春期前孩子参加留宿聚会，应有尽有。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, every parenting decision you make, even the most mundane ones, can feel consequential.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，你做出的每一个育儿决定，哪怕是最琐碎的，都可能让你觉得影响深远。

sentences.en: It's no wonder that many parents feel tired, stressed, and unsure of whether they're doing a good job.
sentences.zh: 难怪许多父母感到疲惫、压力重重，并不确定自己是否做得足够好。

sentences.en: In a recent Pew Research Center survey, 47% of mothers and 34% of fathers said they felt that parenting was tiring most or all of the time,
sentences.zh: 在皮尤研究中心最近的一项调查中，47%的母亲和34%的父亲表示，他们感到育儿在大部分或全部时间里都是令人疲惫的，

sentences.en: and one-third of mothers and one-quarter of fathers felt it was stressful all or most of the time.
sentences.zh: 三分之一的母亲和四分之一的父亲认为育儿在全部或大部分时间里都让人压力倍增。

sentences.en: So as a parent, how do you know which of your choices matter most and where to focus your limited parenting energy?
sentences.zh: 那么作为父母，你如何知道哪些选择最重要，又该将有限的育儿精力集中在哪里呢？

sentences.en: What's the right balance between keeping kids safe and giving them freedom?
sentences.zh: 在保障孩子安全与给予他们自由之间，正确的平衡点在哪里？

sentences.en: How should you respond when your kids try your patience with whining, sibling fights, or teenage sarcasm?
sentences.zh: 当孩子用哭闹、争吵或青少年的冷嘲热讽来考验你的耐心时，你应该如何应对？

sentences.en: How should your parenting change as your kids get older?
sentences.zh: 随着孩子长大，你的育儿方式应该如何改变？

sentences.en: And most important, how can you develop a loving, supportive relationship with your children that will stand the test of time and lead to a happy, well-adjusted family?
sentences.zh: 最重要的是，你如何才能与孩子建立起一种充满爱与支持、经得起时间考验，并能造就一个幸福、适应力强的家庭的关系？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学谈话》，这是美国心理学会的旗舰播客，旨在探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: We have two guests today.
sentences.zh: 今天我们请到了两位嘉宾。

sentences.en: They are the authors of a new book published by the American Psychological Association called Good Enough Parenting, a six-point plan for a stronger relationship with your child.
sentences.zh: 他们是美国心理学会出版的新书《足够好的育儿：建立更强亲子关系的六点计划》的作者。

sentences.en: First is Dr. Tim Cavell, a professor in the Department of Psychological Science at the University of Arkansas and a practicing psychologiSt.
sentences.zh: 第一位是蒂姆·卡维尔博士，他是阿肯色大学心理科学系教授，也是一位执业心理学家。

sentences.en: Dr. Cavell's research focuses on parent and mentor-based interventions for children at risk, including programs for aggressive children and chronically bullied children.
sentences.zh: 卡维尔博士的研究专注于针对高危儿童的家长和导师干预措施，包括针对攻击性儿童和长期遭受霸凌儿童的项目。

sentences.en: Dr. Cavell has also published more than 60 research articles and chapters, as well as several books for clinicians who work with at-risk kids and their families.
sentences.zh: 卡维尔博士还发表了60多篇研究论文和章节，并为从事高危儿童及其家庭工作的临床医生撰写了几本书。

sentences.en: He's also the father of three children who are now in their 20s and 30s.
sentences.zh: 他本人也是三个孩子的父亲，孩子们现在都已经二三十岁了。

sentences.en: Our second guest today is Dr. Lauren Quetch, also a professor in the Department of Psychological Science at the University of Arkansas and a licensed clinical psychologiSt.
sentences.zh: 我们今天的第二位嘉宾是劳伦·奎奇博士，她同样是阿肯色大学心理科学系的教授，也是一位持证临床心理学家。

sentences.en: Her work focuses on children with disruptive behavior and autism spectrum disorder,
sentences.zh: 她的工作重点是患有破坏性行为障碍和自闭症谱系障碍的儿童，

sentences.en: and in particular, helping parents of children with autism build stronger parent-child relationships.
sentences.zh: 特别是帮助自闭症儿童的父母建立更牢固的亲子关系。

sentences.en: She also works with community mental health agencies in an effort to help families get access to evidence-based treatments faster.
sentences.zh: 她还与社区心理健康机构合作，致力于帮助家庭更快地获得循证治疗。

sentences.en: Dr. Quetch is the mother of four young children.
sentences.zh: 奎奇博士是四个年幼孩子的母亲。

sentences.en: Dr. Cavell's and Dr. Quetch's book aims to help the parents of children from toddlers to teens
sentences.zh: 卡维尔博士和奎奇博士的书旨在帮助从幼儿到青少年阶段孩子的父母，

sentences.en: learn practical, science-based strategies to build healthy and lasting parent-child relationships.
sentences.zh: 学习实用的、基于科学的策略，以建立健康且持久的亲子关系。

sentences.en: Thank you both for joining me today.
sentences.zh: 感谢两位今天能来参加节目。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请。

sentences.en: Good to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴来到这里。

sentences.en: Let's start with the title of the book and why you chose it.
sentences.zh: 我们先从书名谈起，说说你们为什么选择这个标题。

sentences.en: What does it mean to be a good enough parent, and why should parents aim for good enough as opposed to spectacular or out of this world?
sentences.zh: 成为一名“足够好的父母”意味着什么？为什么父母应该追求“足够好”，而不是“完美”或“超凡脱俗”？

sentences.en: We must concede that the term was borrowed.
sentences.zh: 我们必须承认，这个词是借用来的。

sentences.en: The phrase good enough mother was coined back in the 50s by a psychologist named Donald Winnicott, and the phrase good enough parenting has been around for quite a while.
sentences.zh: “足够好的母亲”这一说法是由心理学家唐纳德·温尼科特在50年代提出的，而“足够好的育儿”这个概念也已经存在很久了。

sentences.en: In fact, you could probably find two or three books with similar titles that might invoke the term good enough or good enough parenting.
sentences.zh: 事实上，你可能随手就能找到两三本标题类似的书，它们都引用了“足够好”或“足够好的育儿”这一术语。

sentences.en: It's interesting if you look at the history of Winnicott's use of the term because he thought that the perfect parent was less effective than the good enough parent.
sentences.zh: 如果你回顾温尼科特使用这个词的历史，会发现很有意思，因为他认为完美的父母反而不如足够好的父母有效。

sentences.en: And what he meant by that was that the good enough parent doesn't always meet every child's need.
sentences.zh: 他的意思是，足够好的父母并不总是能满足孩子的每一个需求。

sentences.en: In fact, he used the term fail.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他用了“失败”这个词。

sentences.en: Sometimes they fail to meet their child's every need.
sentences.zh: 有时他们确实无法满足孩子的所有需求。

sentences.en: And in so doing, children learn to cope on their own.
sentences.zh: 而正因如此，孩子们学会了独立应对。

sentences.en: And we think that's an important message for today's parent because there's tons of information.
sentences.zh: 我们认为这对当今的父母来说是一个重要的信息，因为现在的信息实在太多了。

sentences.en: To me, it feels like a weight to try to be a good parent.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，试图成为一个“好父母”感觉像是一种负担。

sentences.en: It seems that if the bar has been set to perfect or at least quote unquote effective, and we wanted
sentences.zh: 似乎如果标准被设定为完美，或者至少是所谓的“有效”，而我们想要

sentences.en: to write a book that describes in a more holistic fashion what it means to be a parent that's
sentences.zh: 写一本书，以更全面的方式描述什么是父母，

sentences.en: going to do what matters most and not wear yourself out in the process or not become a hyper hover parent as well.
sentences.zh: 去做最重要的事情，而不是在这个过程中耗尽自己，或者成为那种过度干预的“直升机父母”。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I think when we were talking about this and trying to decide on this title as well, you know, I have four young kids.
sentences.zh: 我想当我们讨论并试图确定这个书名时，你知道，我有四个年幼的孩子。

sentences.en: And one of the things that I've been involved in, I have, there's a group of a few mothers that graduated from my PhD program.
sentences.zh: 我参与过的一件事是，我有一群从我的博士项目中毕业的母亲朋友。

sentences.en: And we all sort of lean on each other for parenting advice, if you will.
sentences.zh: 我们都会互相依靠，寻求育儿建议。

sentences.en: And what ends up happening, what I've realized is a lot of what can be consumed about parenting
sentences.zh: 最终发生的情况是，我意识到关于育儿的很多信息

sentences.en: sets the bar really high to the point of if I do something wrong, what does that mean for my child?
sentences.zh: 把标准定得太高了，以至于如果我做错了一件事，那对我的孩子意味着什么？

sentences.en: My child is going to fail in life.
sentences.zh: 我的孩子这辈子就完了吗？

sentences.en: And this, I've noticed, has created a really high amount of anxiety for new parents in this generation and I think it has really helped to talk to them and sort of bounce ideas off
sentences.zh: 我注意到，这给这一代的新手父母造成了极大的焦虑，我认为与他们交谈并互相交流想法确实很有帮助，

sentences.en: of each other, but also recognize that some of the things that we say are, you know, really important, like, you know, how does my kid look today?
sentences.zh: 但也要认识到我们所说的一些事情，你知道，真的很重要，比如，我的孩子今天看起来怎么样？

sentences.en: Or maybe did I not handle this situation exactly right?
sentences.zh: 或者也许我处理这种情况的方式不够完美？

sentences.en: Comes down to, well, sometimes it's okay to just be good enough.
sentences.zh: 归根结底，有时候做到“足够好”就可以了。

sentences.en: Because if we worry too much about all of the fine details, kind of like what Tim was talking
sentences.zh: 因为如果我们太担心所有细节，就像蒂姆刚才谈到的那样，

sentences.en: about is we miss the larger picture of what it means to be a parent and what it means to run a family.
sentences.zh: 我们就会错过作为父母和经营家庭的全局观。

sentences.en: And so good enough, I think, is often now the advice that parents need more than ever, because
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为“足够好”现在往往是父母比以往任何时候都更需要的建议，因为

sentences.en: they're told so many things about you have to be this way and a perfect parent looks like this and it's just too much.
sentences.zh: 他们被告知了太多事情，比如你必须这样，完美的父母看起来是这样的，这实在太多了。

sentences.en: It's too much to manage.
sentences.zh: 这太难应付了。

sentences.en: Can I add to that?
sentences.zh: 我可以补充一点吗？

sentences.en: Because I agree wholeheartedly with what Lauren said.
sentences.zh: 因为我完全同意劳伦所说的。

sentences.en: And I think our book aims for a sweet spot between, you know, there's one kind of parenting book that's a rather folksy, homespun approach to parenting.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们的书旨在寻找一个平衡点，你知道，有一种育儿书是那种相当通俗、朴实的育儿方法。

sentences.en: It's more of a literary work than a reflection of the science of parenting.
sentences.zh: 它更像是一部文学作品，而不是对育儿科学的反映。

sentences.en: Then there are those books that are drawn tightly from the science of parenting, but those can get rather prescriptive and exacting.
sentences.zh: 还有一些书是严格取材于育儿科学，但那些书往往过于教条和苛刻。

sentences.en: And our book, I think, is aimed sort of between the two at a sweet spot, which says, let's
sentences.zh: 而我们的书，我认为是瞄准了两者之间的平衡点，它说，让我们

sentences.en: build from, let's draw from the science of parenting, but let's render it in a way that's user-friendly,
sentences.zh: 建立在育儿科学的基础上，但要以一种用户友好、

sentences.en: that's parent-friendly, that's digestible, and that distills the key findings down to an essential whole, to what matters moSt.
sentences.zh: 对父母友好、易于消化，并将关键发现提炼成一个本质整体的方式呈现，专注于最重要的事情。

sentences.en: Does the good enough approach, in effect, also extend to the kids?
sentences.zh: 这种“足够好”的方法，实际上是否也适用于孩子？

sentences.en: Because, you know, there's so much pressure on our children these days to be absolutely perfect and spectacular.
sentences.zh: 因为，你知道，如今我们的孩子承受着巨大的压力，必须绝对完美和出色。

sentences.en: So if you're a good enough parent, well, maybe you can be a good enough son or daughter as well.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你是一个足够好的父母，那么也许你也可以成为一个足够好的儿子或女儿。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: I think sometimes people don't realize that when you set standards really high for yourself
sentences.zh: 我认为有时人们没有意识到，当你为自己

sentences.en: or for your child, like, I want my child to be the greatest athlete there ever was, right?
sentences.zh: 或为孩子设定极高的标准时，比如，我希望我的孩子成为有史以来最伟大的运动员，对吧？

sentences.en: And now I know what it means.
sentences.zh: 现在我知道这意味着什么了。

sentences.en: That means they need to be involved in three sports that take up all their time and the
sentences.zh: 这意味着他们需要参加三项占用所有时间的运动，还要上

sentences.en: AP classes.
sentences.zh: 大学预修课程（AP）。

sentences.en: They need to be involved in all of those because my child's going to be the beSt.
sentences.zh: 他们需要参与所有这些，因为我的孩子要成为最棒的。

sentences.en: And what ends up happening is the child gets burnt out, the parent can get burnt out.
sentences.zh: 最终的结果是孩子精疲力竭，父母也可能精疲力竭。

sentences.en: And when you base your family and your relationship off of those accomplishments, rather than the relationship you actually have with one another, you lose something in there.
sentences.zh: 当你把家庭和关系建立在这些成就之上，而不是你们彼此之间实际拥有的关系上时，你就失去了一些东西。

sentences.en: And that can cause more distress rather than just focusing on, again, what matters most, the good enough.
sentences.zh: 这可能会导致更多的痛苦，而不是仅仅专注于——再说一次——最重要的事情，即“足够好”。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I think it's been way overstated that our parenting shapes our children and their personality and their future.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，我们的育儿方式塑造了孩子、他们的个性和未来，这种说法被严重夸大了。

sentences.en: There are a lot of other factors besides parenting practices that shape who children become.
sentences.zh: 除了育儿实践之外，还有许多其他因素塑造了孩子的成长。

sentences.en: And more recent research speaks loudly to that.
sentences.zh: 最近的研究有力地证明了这一点。

sentences.en: And as a parent, my tendency is to adopt a posture of discovery.
sentences.zh: 作为父母，我的倾向是采取一种“探索”的姿态。

sentences.en: Let me discover who my children will become.
sentences.zh: 让我去发现我的孩子将会成为什么样的人。

sentences.en: And let me be ready to love and accept them when I discover who they are.
sentences.zh: 当我发现他们是谁时，让我准备好去爱和接纳他们。

sentences.en: But the notion that I'm exercising my preferences and shaping who they are and who they become is both mythical and dangerous.
sentences.zh: 但那种认为我是在行使我的偏好并塑造他们是谁以及他们将成为什么样的人的想法，既是神话，也是危险的。

sentences.en: So, it's an interesting posture to adopt, but I think it's a healthy one.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是一种有趣的姿态，但我认为这是一种健康的姿态。

sentences.en: Let me learn who my child is.
sentences.zh: 让我去了解我的孩子是谁。

sentences.en: Let me learn who my child will become.
sentences.zh: 让我去了解我的孩子将成为什么样的人。

sentences.en: And let me practice accepting who that child is and conveying a message of love and belonging.
sentences.zh: 让我练习接纳那个孩子，并传达爱与归属感的信息。

sentences.en: That's a different way to go about the task of parenting.
sentences.zh: 这是进行育儿任务的一种不同方式。

sentences.en: And I think that that segues into the question that I had, where you write about the most important job that parents have is to build a relationship with their children.
sentences.zh: 我想这引出了我的问题，你们在书中写道，父母最重要的工作是与孩子建立关系。

sentences.en: And I think that might surprise some people maybe who don't think that they need to build a relationship because they have a relationship.
sentences.zh: 我想这可能会让一些人感到惊讶，因为他们可能认为自己不需要建立关系，因为他们已经有了关系。

sentences.en: But what do you mean?
sentences.zh: 但你们是什么意思？

sentences.en: What is the special approach that you recommend that might not be immediately evident to a harried mother or father?
sentences.zh: 你们推荐的这种特殊方法是什么，对于忙碌的母亲或父亲来说，可能不是显而易见的？

sentences.en: So, I believe that we've got core components that we highlight within this book.
sentences.zh: 所以，我相信我们在书中强调了核心组成部分。

sentences.en: There are three aspects that we believe are really important for a relationship between a parent and a child.
sentences.zh: 我们认为对于亲子关系来说，有三个方面非常重要。

sentences.en: And then we also have some components that we feel are sort of the foundations of those things, too.
sentences.zh: 然后我们还有一些我们认为也是这些事情基础的组成部分。

sentences.en: So, largely, when we're thinking about a relationship, which Tim alluded to already previously, was this posture of acceptance.
sentences.zh: 所以，很大程度上，当我们思考关系时，正如蒂姆之前提到的，就是这种“接纳”的姿态。

sentences.en: So, when we think about our relationship with our child, we're really saying, I see you and I accept who you are for who you are, right?
sentences.zh: 所以，当我们思考与孩子的关系时，我们实际上是在说，我看见你，我接纳你本来的样子，对吧？

sentences.en: So, I have four little children, and I may parent them pretty similarly.
sentences.zh: 我有四个年幼的孩子，我可能以非常相似的方式养育他们。

sentences.en: You know, they're all close in age together as well.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们的年龄也很接近。

sentences.en: And they are different.
sentences.zh: 但他们是不同的人。

sentences.en: They're different people.
sentences.zh: 他们是不同的人。

sentences.en: They have different interests.
sentences.zh: 他们有不同的兴趣。

sentences.en: They have different inclinations.
sentences.zh: 他们有不同的倾向。

sentences.en: They have different temperaments.
sentences.zh: 他们有不同的气质。

sentences.en: And so, part of being a parent then is first saying, I see that you are who you are, and I'm okay with that.
sentences.zh: 所以，作为父母的一部分就是首先说，我看到你就是你，我对此没问题。

sentences.en: And that can look in many different ways.
sentences.zh: 这可以表现为许多不同的方式。

sentences.en: It can be very outward in the way that we express that, and it can also be more silent in the way that we express that, too.
sentences.zh: 它可以是我们表达方式中非常外向的，也可以是我们表达方式中更沉默的。

sentences.en: So, sometimes not saying anything, rather than correcting your child all the time.
sentences.zh: 所以，有时候什么都不说，而不是一直纠正你的孩子。

sentences.en: The second component of that then is containing.
sentences.zh: 那么第二个组成部分就是“约束”。

sentences.en: So, thinking about our job as a parent is also to recognize that we, you know, children are impulsive sometimes.
sentences.zh: 所以，思考我们作为父母的工作，也是要认识到，你知道，孩子有时是冲动的。

sentences.en: We still have to welcome them into the culture and society in which we live and tell them what is and is not acceptable.
sentences.zh: 我们仍然必须欢迎他们进入我们所生活的文化和社会，并告诉他们什么是可以接受的，什么是不可以接受的。

sentences.en: And so, our practices of containment sort of help us do that.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们的约束实践在某种程度上帮助我们做到这一点。

sentences.en: And then the last component within that is being a leader and your leadership within the family.
sentences.zh: 那么其中的最后一个组成部分就是成为领导者，以及你在家庭中的领导力。

sentences.en: So, outwardly expressing what it means to be a good person, talking about what our values are within a family, and then sharing that with our children, too.
sentences.zh: 所以，外在地表达成为一个好人意味着什么，谈论我们在家庭中的价值观是什么，然后也与我们的孩子分享这些。

sentences.en: There's more to that, and I'll let Tim take over.
sentences.zh: 还有更多内容，我让蒂姆接着说。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: I think if we zoom back a little bit, I think there needs to be an appreciation that we have
sentences.zh: 我想如果我们稍微退后一点，我认为需要有一种认识，即我们

sentences.en: cast, we being mainly professionals like Lauren and I, have tended to cast parenting as something set apart from relationships.
sentences.zh: ——我们主要是像劳伦和我这样的专业人士——倾向于将育儿视为与关系分开的事情。

sentences.en: There are some parenting advice that's like an itemized list of, if your child does X, you should do Y.
sentences.zh: 有些育儿建议就像是一份逐项清单，如果你的孩子做了X，你应该做Y。

sentences.en: If your child has this problem or engages in this behavior, and this is how you should respond
sentences.zh: 如果你的孩子有这个问题或从事这种行为，这就是你应该如何回应，

sentences.en: without appreciating the context of the relationship in which those events occur, you know, depending
sentences.zh: 而没有考虑到这些事件发生的关系背景，你知道，取决于

sentences.en: on how strong or strained the relationship is, you might want to do very different things
sentences.zh: 关系的强弱或紧张程度，你可能想做非常不同的事情，

sentences.en: because at the end of the day, it's the relationship that will move your child toward being a good, healthy citizen.
sentences.zh: 因为归根结底，是这种关系推动你的孩子成为一个优秀、健康的公民。

sentences.en: And I tend to say it this way, Kim, if there was some farcical choice I had to make between
sentences.zh: 我倾向于这样说，金，如果我必须在

sentences.en: two surrogate parents, one who was very good at relationships in his or her life, and one
sentences.zh: 两个代理父母之间做出某种荒谬的选择，一个是生活中非常擅长处理关系的人，一个是

sentences.en: who knew a lot about parenting, I would choose the one who was good at relationships, okay?
sentences.zh: 非常了解育儿知识的人，我会选择那个擅长处理关系的人，好吗？

sentences.en: Because that's what it is.
sentences.zh: 因为这就是本质。

sentences.en: But too often, I think because of people like us throwing out so much advice, folks become parents, and they move into this mode where they sort of jettison what they think about
sentences.zh: 但太频繁了，我认为因为像我们这样的人抛出了太多的建议，人们成为父母，他们进入了一种模式，他们抛弃了关于如何让关系运作的想法。

sentences.en: in terms of how to make a relationship work.
sentences.zh: 我们拥有的任何关系都不应该涉及被伤害、被利用、被虐待。

sentences.en: None of the relationships we have should involve being victimized, taken advantage of, being abused.
sentences.zh: 我们拥有的任何关系都不应该涉及不去尝试向我们爱和关心的人传达接纳的信息。

sentences.en: None of the relationships we have should involve not trying to convey a message of acceptance to the people we love and care about.
sentences.zh: 我们拥有的任何关系都不应该涉及放弃我们的核心价值观，以及我们如何为人处世。

sentences.en: And none of the relationships we have should involve abandoning what our core values are, how we carry ourselves.
sentences.zh: 所以你想把所有这些关系的组成部分带入亲子关系中，

sentences.en: So you want to bring all those relationship components to the parent-child relationship,
sentences.zh: 不仅仅因为它是亲子关系，而是因为这就是拥有健康关系意味着什么。

sentences.en: not just because it's a parent-child relationship, because that's what it means to have a healthy relationship.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 在书的开头，你们要求父母思考他们的育儿目标，这与他们对孩子未来的目标不同。

sentences.en: At the beginning of the book, you ask parents to think about their parenting goals, which are not the same as the goals that they might have for their children's future.
sentences.zh: 当你们谈论育儿目标时，是什么意思？

sentences.en: What do you mean when you talk about parenting goals?
sentences.zh: 父母应该如何设定这些目标，又如何坚持下去？

sentences.en: How should parents set them and how can they stick to them?
sentences.zh: 这是一个很好的问题。

sentences.en: That's a great question.
sentences.zh: 我们将育儿目标描述为父母为指导其育儿行为而设定的目标。

sentences.en: We describe parenting goals as the goals parents have for guiding their parenting behavior.
sentences.zh: 但这很少成为讨论的话题。

sentences.en: But it's seldom a topic of discussion.
sentences.zh: 你的育儿目标是什么？

sentences.en: What are your parenting goals?
sentences.zh: 再说一次，我们倾向于从我们对孩子未来的期望角度来思考它。

sentences.en: Again, we tend to think of it in terms of what we want for our children downstream.
sentences.zh: 但那不是育儿目标。

sentences.en: But if you are a parent, a working parent, you go home that evening, you have some goals in mind as a parent.
sentences.zh: 但如果你是一位家长，一位职场家长，那天晚上回到家时，你作为家长心中会有一些目标。

sentences.en: Oftentimes, they're sort of hidden and maybe embedded in automatic reactions to children.
sentences.zh: 通常，这些目标是隐藏的，可能潜藏在对孩子自动化的反应之中。

sentences.en: Things become sort of mindless and routine.
sentences.zh: 事情变得有些不经大脑且流于常规。

sentences.en: And we may not be forward-thinking or conscious about, what are we trying to do in these interactions I have with my child?
sentences.zh: 我们可能并没有前瞻性或自觉地去思考：在我和孩子的这些互动中，我到底想要达成什么？

sentences.en: And if there's value in having a relationship where children feel accepted, they are periodically contained.
sentences.zh: 如果建立一种让孩子感到被接纳的关系是有价值的，那么他们也会定期受到约束。

sentences.en: In other words, there's a message of this you cannot do.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，这传达了一个“你不能这样做”的信息。

sentences.en: And the parent is carrying himself or herself in a way that espouses good values.
sentences.zh: 而家长以一种推崇良好价值观的方式来要求自己。

sentences.en: Then those are great goals to guide parenting behavior.
sentences.zh: 那么这些就是指导育儿行为的伟大目标。

sentences.en: Now, will you know the outcome immediately in terms of your children's functioning?
sentences.zh: 那么，你能立即看到孩子表现方面的结果吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不能。

sentences.en: It's like a plan.
sentences.zh: 这就像一个计划。

sentences.en: It takes time for that to unfold.
sentences.zh: 这需要时间来展现。

sentences.en: So, the goals for parenting behavior are more proximal to what we do in any given day or situation.
sentences.zh: 所以，育儿行为的目标与我们在任何特定日子或情况下所做的事情更为贴近。

sentences.en: And to add on that too, when we act automatically, we may be doing ourselves harm in that relationship.
sentences.zh: 此外还要补充一点，当我们自动行事时，我们可能会在那种关系中伤害到自己。

sentences.en: And so, thinking about our goal as just having a stronger relationship with our child rather than worrying about who they're going to be or are they the smartest kid in the class?
sentences.zh: 因此，与其担心孩子将来会成为什么样的人，或者他们是不是班上最聪明的孩子，不如把目标设定为与孩子建立更牢固的关系。

sentences.en: Are they the best athlete?
sentences.zh: 他们是最好的运动员吗？

sentences.en: Are they the best dressed?
sentences.zh: 他们穿得最好吗？

sentences.en: Are they going to be X, Y, and Z?
sentences.zh: 他们会成为这样那样的人吗？

sentences.en: That may snap in as an automatic goal that you're not thinking about where you're snarky with your kid or you're telling them what they need to be doing.
sentences.zh: 这可能会成为一个你并未察觉的自动目标，导致你对孩子尖酸刻薄，或者不停地告诉他们该做什么。

sentences.en: And that sort of forces your hand sometimes to say, how hard am I going to push if my kid isn't doing what I want them to do right now?
sentences.zh: 这有时会迫使你不得不去想：如果我的孩子现在不按我说的做，我到底要逼他们到什么程度？

sentences.en: I may be pushing an agenda I'm not even aware of consciously at the expense of the relationship that I have with my child.
sentences.zh: 我可能在推行一个我甚至没有意识到的议程，而代价却是我与孩子之间的关系。

sentences.en: And so, if my goal is, maybe I'm struggling with the relationship with my child right now.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果我的目标是——也许我目前正为与孩子的关系而苦恼。

sentences.en: So, if my goal, if I'm conscious about, I care about my child feeling loved and wanting them to love me back too.
sentences.zh: 那么，如果我的目标是——如果我有意识地关注这一点，我关心的是让孩子感受到爱，并希望他们也爱我。

sentences.en: Obviously, you can't make your child do anything in that way.
sentences.zh: 显然，你无法以那种方式强迫孩子做任何事。

sentences.en: You can't force them to love you.
sentences.zh: 你无法强迫他们爱你。

sentences.en: And yet, if you have that goal of, I want us to be stronger together and you're more thoughtful about it, that can change how you act in a moment.
sentences.zh: 然而，如果你有“我希望我们在一起更亲密”这个目标，并且对此更加深思熟虑，那就能改变你当下的行为。

sentences.en: And so, cleaning up the floor or addressing the tone in which they spoke back to you may seem like that's the most important thing if we're thinking automatically in that moment.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果我们当时是自动反应，清理地板或纠正他们回话的语气似乎就是最重要的事情。

sentences.en: But if we say, my relationship is the most important, our relationship together is the most important, then maybe you let some of those things go and that actually ends up building
sentences.zh: 但如果我们说，我的关系是最重要的，我们在一起的关系是最重要的，那么也许你会放过其中一些事情，而这最终反而会建立起

sentences.en: that relationship stronger.
sentences.zh: 更牢固的关系。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's being intentional, deliberate, and explicit with why you're doing what you're
sentences.zh: 是的，这就是作为家长要做到有意识、深思熟虑且明确你所做之事的理由，

sentences.en: doing as a parent as opposed to reacting out of some hidden emotional goal like I'm frustrated or I'm tired or out of some preference to live vicariously through your child.
sentences.zh: 而不是出于某种隐藏的情绪目标（比如我很沮丧或我很累），或者出于某种想通过孩子来实现自己未竟愿望的偏好而做出反应。

sentences.en: So, if the, and we offer to parents that, you know, useful goals to keep in mind are conveying
sentences.zh: 所以，如果——我们向家长建议，你知道，要记住的有用目标是传达

sentences.en: a message of acceptance, conveying a message of containment, that there are some things you
sentences.zh: 一种接纳的信息，传达一种约束的信息，即有些事情你

sentences.en: cannot do, and then conveying a message of what our family values, what we believe in and hold dear.
sentences.zh: 不能做，然后传达一种关于我们家庭价值观、我们信仰和珍视之物的信息。

sentences.en: So, let me pick up from what you've just said, because you're talking about containment rather than discipline.
sentences.zh: 那么，让我接着你刚才说的话讲，因为你谈到的是约束而不是管教。

sentences.en: And in the book, you offer a rule of thumb.
sentences.zh: 在书中，你提供了一个经验法则。

sentences.en: You call it the 80-20 rule.
sentences.zh: 你称之为“80-20法则”。

sentences.en: What is that, and how does that work?
sentences.zh: 那是什么，它是如何运作的？

sentences.en: So, we make the provocative point that effective discipline is selective discipline, okay?
sentences.zh: 我们提出了一个挑衅性的观点：有效的管教是有选择性的管教，明白吗？

sentences.en: Now, there's a lot of science on inept, what Jerry Patterson and colleagues at Oregon Social
sentences.zh: 关于无能的管教，俄勒冈社会学习中心的杰瑞·帕特森（Jerry Patterson）及其同事过去常称之为对行为具有破坏性和挑衅性的儿童进行无能的管教，

sentences.en: Learning Center used to call inept discipline with children whose behavior was disruptive and defiant.
sentences.zh: 这方面有很多科学研究。

sentences.en: And the pattern that was observed in these parents was of two sorts, either being quite harsh and overly punitive or being quite lax and permissive, okay?
sentences.zh: 在这些家长身上观察到的模式有两种：要么非常严厉和过度惩罚，要么非常松懈和放任，明白吗？

sentences.en: Not unlike, you know, Balmerin's distinction.
sentences.zh: 这和鲍姆林德（Baumrind）的区分没什么两样。

sentences.en: So, and it makes sense if you're a parent who's having trouble controlling your child's behavior,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你是一位在控制孩子行为方面遇到困难的家长，这很有道理，

sentences.en: then you might wax and wane between being permissive and harsh, harsh and permissive.
sentences.zh: 那么你可能会在放任和严厉、严厉和放任之间摇摆不定。

sentences.en: And so, it can be countered by having clarity about, well, what are the things that matter most?
sentences.zh: 因此，通过明确“什么才是最重要的事”，可以抵消这种摇摆。

sentences.en: What are the things that you want to be consistent on in terms of being a disciplinarian?
sentences.zh: 在管教方面，你想要坚持的事情是什么？

sentences.en: And what things do you let go?
sentences.zh: 而哪些事情你可以放手？

sentences.en: Sometimes it's said in the parenting literature, Kim, is choose your battles wisely, right?
sentences.zh: 育儿文献中常说，金（Kim），要明智地选择你的战场，对吧？

sentences.en: It's a very common phrase.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常常见的短语。

sentences.en: It's a bit unfortunate that the word battle is in there.
sentences.zh: 有点遗憾的是里面用了“战场”这个词。

sentences.en: But nonetheless, the point about choosing wisely is well-founded.
sentences.zh: 但尽管如此，关于明智选择的观点是有充分根据的。

sentences.en: But it's not often talked about, like, well, what does that mean, you know, choose your battle wisely?
sentences.zh: 但人们并不常讨论，比如，你知道，“明智地选择你的战场”到底是什么意思？

sentences.en: Well, we think that the science of parenting points us in a direction there in developmental psychology.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们认为发展心理学中的育儿科学为我们指明了方向。

sentences.en: One of the behaviors that is most problematic for children's development is their use of coercion, which is a broad term used to define various forms of aggression or antagonistic
sentences.zh: 对儿童发展最成问题的行为之一是他们对强制手段的使用，这是一个广义术语，用于定义各种形式的攻击或对抗性

sentences.en: or threatening behavior, okay?
sentences.zh: 或威胁性行为，明白吗？

sentences.en: Children who learn to use coercion, aggression, and other sorts of antagonistic behavior are at risk for a lot of problems downstream.
sentences.zh: 学会使用强制、攻击和其他对抗性行为的儿童，在未来面临很多问题的风险。

sentences.en: School dropout, delinquency, substance use, things like that.
sentences.zh: 辍学、犯罪、药物滥用等等。

sentences.en: And so, clearly, this is a category that matters most, that matters a lot.
sentences.zh: 所以，显然，这是一个最重要、影响巨大的类别。

sentences.en: So, if you're looking for where to put your time and energy, it makes sense to put your time and energy on limiting your child's use of coercion and aggression.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你在寻找该把时间和精力放在哪里，把时间和精力放在限制孩子使用强制和攻击行为上是有意义的。

sentences.en: Now, there are a whole host of other things that matter little to children's development.
sentences.zh: 现在，还有一大堆对儿童发展影响甚微的事情。

sentences.en: I think we give an example in the book of bacon eating.
sentences.zh: 我想我们在书中举了一个吃培根的例子。

sentences.en: You know, what if your daughter was eating bacon, and only bacon, and just, it persisted, and you said, well, you got to eat something else, and that's all she ate.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果你的女儿在吃培根，而且只吃培根，并且一直这样，你说，好吧，你得吃点别的，但她只吃那个。

sentences.en: So, at what point does bacon eating rise to a significant problem?
sentences.zh: 那么，吃培根在什么时候会上升为一个重大问题？

sentences.en: It might take a while before that's a significant problem.
sentences.zh: 在它成为重大问题之前可能需要一段时间。

sentences.en: There's a lot of things that we as parents can prefer that our children not do that we find maybe disgusting or, you know, unsightly, or that it might be annoying.
sentences.zh: 作为家长，我们可能更希望孩子不要做很多事情，我们可能觉得这些事情令人作呕，或者，你知道，不雅观，或者可能很烦人。

sentences.en: But that's very different than saying this behavior, if repeated, has developmental significance.
sentences.zh: 但这与说“这种行为如果重复发生，具有发展意义”是完全不同的。

sentences.en: There are not many of those to pay attention to, but the ones that aren't, you really want to pay attention to it.
sentences.zh: 需要注意的事情并不多，但那些需要注意的事情，你真的要留心。

sentences.en: And here's the kicker.
sentences.zh: 关键就在这里。

sentences.en: If you're going after, let's say, hypothetically,
sentences.zh: 如果你打算处理，比方说，假设有

sentences.en: 20 different behaviors, only two of which matter, and you're going to be spreading thin your efforts to discipline and contain, and likely fail.
sentences.zh: 20种不同的行为，其中只有两种很重要，那么你就会分散你在管教和约束方面的精力，而且很可能会失败。

sentences.en: And so, you actually dilute your authority.
sentences.zh: 所以，你实际上稀释了自己的权威。

sentences.en: You dilute the degree to which children see you as a person of authority, because you're not being effective, and because you're trying to do too much.
sentences.zh: 你稀释了孩子将你视为权威人物的程度，因为你没有成效，而且因为你试图做的事情太多了。

sentences.en: Okay?
sentences.zh: 明白吗？

sentences.en: And so, you want to preserve your efforts at containment for things that matter moSt. We actually, some of my research looked at
sentences.zh: 所以，你要把约束的精力保留给那些最重要的事情。实际上，我的一些研究观察了

sentences.en: children's beliefs about whether parents and teachers can contain them if there's a conflict in goals.
sentences.zh: 孩子们关于如果目标冲突时，家长和老师是否能约束他们的信念。

sentences.en: We had a measure, and one of the items was something like, you want to go play outside.
sentences.zh: 我们有一个衡量标准，其中一个项目是这样的：你想去外面玩。

sentences.en: Your mom says you can't go play outside.
sentences.zh: 你妈妈说你不能去外面玩。

sentences.en: Can she make you stay inside?
sentences.zh: 她能让你待在里面吗？

sentences.en: So, it's an effort to get it.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是一种尝试去了解。

sentences.en: Do children believe that adults are in charge?
sentences.zh: 孩子们是否相信成年人说了算？

sentences.en: Well, lo and behold, most kids say, yes, they're in charge.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你瞧，大多数孩子说，是的，他们说了算。

sentences.en: But for the kids who doubt that, for the kids who have a low sense of containment, they had high levels of problem behavior, regardless of how well parents discipline.
sentences.zh: 但对于那些怀疑这一点的孩子，对于那些对约束感较低的孩子，无论家长管教得多么好，他们都有高水平的问题行为。

sentences.en: So, if children are operating from a belief that I can outwit you, you know, do a turnaround, and I can work around you, if they doubt your position of authority, that's not good.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果孩子们基于“我可以胜过你”的信念行事，你知道，来个大反转，我可以绕过你，如果他们怀疑你的权威地位，那可不好。

sentences.en: And so, you want to protect and preserve your position of authority through the use of selective discipline.
sentences.zh: 因此，你要通过选择性管教来保护和维护你的权威地位。

sentences.en: The other win that comes from that is that you reduce the number of occasions where the interactions are emotionally negative,
sentences.zh: 由此带来的另一个好处是，你减少了互动中情绪负面的次数，

sentences.en: because discipline can often involve negative emotionality, unpleasant encounters.
sentences.zh: 因为管教往往涉及负面情绪、不愉快的遭遇。

sentences.en: So, if you reduce the occasions where you're trying to discipline your child to contain your child where there's negative emotions, then guess what happens?
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你减少了试图管教孩子、约束孩子而产生负面情绪的次数，那么猜猜会发生什么？

sentences.en: Your relationship is more positive than negative.
sentences.zh: 你们的关系会变得积极多于消极。

sentences.en: And again, there's pretty consistent research that shows that an 80% or about four to one ratio
sentences.zh: 同样，有相当一致的研究表明，80%或大约四比一的比例，

sentences.en: of positive or neutral exchanges to negative exchanges signals a satisfying, stable relationship.
sentences.zh: 即积极或中性交流与消极交流的比例，标志着一种令人满意、稳定的关系。

sentences.en: If you're a parent who's at 50%, half the time it's negative, half the time it's positive, that's not good.

sentences.en: stupid or unwise.

sentences.en: Mindful parenting, on the other hand, it involves a much more conscious, deliberate, effortful decision about what you're going to do.

sentences.zh: 但你有时可以进入那种模式。

sentences.zh: 对于那些气质温和、作息规律、顺从、合作且情绪稳定的孩子，

sentences.en: For children who are easy temperament, meet schedules, they're compliant, cooperative, they're emotionally regulated.
sentences.zh: 我认为亲子关系同样需要那三个条件，即包含和引导。

sentences.en: Parenting, I think the parent-child relationship is going to have the same three conditions except contain and lead.
sentences.zh: 但父母不需要那么费力、那么刻意，就能相当容易地做到这一点。

sentences.en: But parents won't have to work as hard as deliberately and it will be fairly easy to pull that off.
sentences.zh: 当你面对一个具有挑战性的孩子时，你必须在尝试做的事情上更加刻意、清醒和明确。

sentences.en: When you have a challenging child, you have to be more intentional and conscious and explicit about what you're trying to do.
sentences.zh: 温尼科特（Winnicott）创造了“足够好的母亲”这个词，他非常推崇普通的父母、普通的母亲，因为他看到了普通父母身上有许多优点。

sentences.en: Winnicott, who coined the term good enough mother, was a big fan of ordinary parents, ordinary mothers, in the sense that he saw in ordinary parents so many strengths.
sentences.zh: 我认为随着时间的推移，我们这个领域在某种程度上把育儿描绘得非同寻常，将其视为一套独立的技能，你未必天生具备，

sentences.en: And I think our field over time has sort of cast parenting as extraordinary, as something as a separate set of skills that you don't, you're not necessarily equipped with,
sentences.zh: 而必须去查阅某本书或咨询某位专家。

sentences.en: that you have to go to some book or some expert for.
sentences.zh: 我们愿意相信，如果你能处理好你的人际关系，包括与孩子的关系，你就会做得很好。

sentences.en: We'd like to believe that if you can manage well your relationships, including the one with your child, you're going to be fine.
sentences.zh: 但要认识到，对于某些孩子来说，这项任务会更具挑战性，看起来也会略有不同。

sentences.en: But recognize that for some children, the task is going to be more challenging and it's going to look a little different.
sentences.zh: 让我们用最后一个问题来结束吧。

sentences.en: Let's close with this one question.
sentences.zh: 我要依次问你们两位，对于你们每个人来说，有一条你们想留给听众的育儿建议是什么？

sentences.en: I'm going to throw it at both of you sequentially, which is for each of you, what is one piece of parenting advice that you would like to leave with our listeners?
sentences.zh: 我在书的开头谈到过一件事，当 Tim 找我一起写这本书时，这是我脑海中浮现的第一件事，

sentences.en: One of the things that I talk about within the beginning of the book, which when Tim approached me about writing this together, this is the first thing that came to my
sentences.zh: 当我刚开始学习如何成为一名临床心理学家时，它真的深深印在了我的脑海里。

sentences.en: mind and really stuck with me when I was first learning how to be a clinical psychologiSt.
sentences.zh: 所以我先讲这个轶事，然后用我所表达的意思来总结。

sentences.en: So I'll give you this antidote and then I'll sort of end with what I mean by it all.
sentences.zh: 当时有一位母亲带着她的小男孩来找我，她在寻求服务时凑近我对我说：“我爱我的孩子，但我并不喜欢我的孩子。”

sentences.en: So I had a parent come in and she had a young boy and she leaned in close to me when she was trying to seek services and she said, I love my child, but I don't like my child.
sentences.zh: 这句话在我脑海中停留了很久，直到我有了自己的孩子，才终于连接并理解了它的含义。

sentences.en: And it stuck with me for so long and it took a long time for me to connect and understand what that meant finally when I had my own children.
sentences.zh: 但我认为重点在于，作为父母，有很多事情你可以努力去做。

sentences.en: But I think the point being here that there are many things that you can work on as a parent.
sentences.zh: 我们总是可以做得更好，为我们的孩子寻求更多。

sentences.en: We can always do better and seek for more for our children.
sentences.zh: 然而，如果我们能以爱为先，如果我们能记住，归根结底，我们的任务是爱我们的孩子，陪伴在他们身边，

sentences.en: And yet if we can lead with love and if we can remember that at the end of the day, our task is to love our children and be there
sentences.zh: 接纳他们，我认为这是在担心其他任何事情之前最需要做的事情。

sentences.en: for them and accept them, I think that is the biggest thing that needs to happen first before you worry about anything else.
sentences.zh: 所以我们对孩子有很多期望。

sentences.en: And so there are many things we want for our children.
sentences.zh: 我们对孩子有很多希望。

sentences.en: There are many things we hope for, for our children.
sentences.zh: 如果我们能接纳他们本来的样子，接纳他们所处的阶段，我认为这是作为父母在尝试做任何其他事情之前，

sentences.en: And if we just can accept them for who they are and where they're at, I think that is the first, the first thing you have to accomplish as a parent before you can
sentences.zh: 必须完成的第一件事。

sentences.en: try to do anything else.

sentences.en: Dr. Cavell?
sentences.zh: 育儿涉及头脑和心灵，或者说是科学与艺术，如果你愿意这样称呼的话。

sentences.en: Parenting involves the head and the heart or science and art, if you will.
sentences.zh: 所以有些父母有时在情感层面投入过多。

sentences.en: And so some parents sometimes lead too much with what's happening emotionally.
sentences.zh: 而有些父母则试图遵循他们认为正确的科学方法。

sentences.en: The science tells us this, there are some things that are important and try to emphasize those things.
sentences.zh: 我们的书也谈到了这一点。

sentences.en: And our book speaks to that.
sentences.zh: 还有很多事情并不那么重要。

sentences.en: And there are a lot of things that are not, that don't matter that much.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你想运用你的头脑或育儿科学，请认识到并非所有事情都有后果。

sentences.en: And so if you want to use your mind or the science of parenting, recognize that not everything is consequential.
sentences.zh: 事实上，育儿科学会强烈建议你，当你决定把精力放在哪里时，请放在亲子关系上。

sentences.en: In fact, the science of parenting would say to you very strongly, when you go to decide where to put your energies, put it on the relationship.
sentences.zh: 那是你应该加倍投入的地方。

sentences.en: That's where you double down.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你在纠结：我应该让孩子面壁思过吗？

sentences.en: Pay attention to the relationship.

sentences.zh: 我之所以这样建议，是因为我认为父母通常不会在第一时间去评估关系的质量。

sentences.en: And I offer that because I don't think assessing the quality of the relationship is often what parents typically go to early.
sentences.zh: 相反，他们是在寻找解决某个问题的快速答案，而不是问：“我和我的孩子现在怎么样？”

sentences.en: Instead, they're looking for a quick answer to some, to fix some problem as opposed to saying, how are we doing my child and I?
sentences.zh: 我能做些什么来让这种关系变得牢固？

sentences.en: What can I do to make that relationship strong?
sentences.zh: 也许我需要，它需要以某种方式修复吗？

sentences.en: Maybe do I need to, does it, does it need to be repaired in some way?
sentences.zh: 我在情感上是否难以对孩子保持耐心和投入？

sentences.en: What do I need to do to be an emotionally healthy parent so I can have a better relationship with my child?
sentences.zh: 所以这是一种不同的育儿思维方式，不要把它看作是一份需要不断修补的工作，而是一段你需要经营 18 年以上的关系。

sentences.en: So it's, it's a different way to think about parenting, not as a job where you look at an endless series of fixes, but it's about a relationship that you manage 18 plus years.
